result:
Round 93 passes with 0 bugs. It was checked in a real browser at both viewports, so `browserVerified` and `realVerified` are both true. The three Low bugs (GATE91-S1, A-R86-L7, A-R86-L8) can close. I made no changes to app source.

**Source state:** HEAD is still `64e12d8`, with the expected 2 modified and 2 new files. All 518 frozen files are unchanged, and A's and the protected file hashes match. Every changed region of the dialog is inside what B granted, and doc 080 changed only on line 4.

**What I tested** (Playwright Chromium, a new private window per session, no login):
- **Screen-reader names (1280 and 1440):** I read Chrome's accessibility tree for every radio in three states: no range, a 4–9 s range, and the loop turned on. Each radio's name and description match B's table exactly, and the WAV note text follows the scope and loop state. No note text leaks into any radio's name. With a valid range, the range radio gets no description, so Chrome does not fall back to reading the label text.
- **Clicking the text:** clicking the MP3 name, the WAV + MP3 note and the WAV name each selects that format, and the Export button text changes to match.
- **Master-mute note (both viewports):** it says WAV, MP3 or WAV + MP3 according to the selected format, in whole-project and 4–9 s range scope. After closing and reopening, it is back to WAV.
- **No-sound note:** I reached it in the real browser rather than leaving it to unit tests, by importing our own test video with no audio track as the only clip. All three format texts are exact in project scope, and MP3 is exact in range scope.
- **Layout:** in each option the name is one line with the note below it. The WAV + MP3 option measures exactly what round 91 measured. Its label text is also byte-identical to round 91's.
- **Export still works:**
  - WAV of the whole project at 1280: a valid 24-bit, 48 kHz stereo file. Its length is exactly the project length, 101.702 s.
  - MP3 of the 4–9 s range at 1440: it decodes to 48 kHz stereo, 5.000 s long.
  - The clipping warning that appears is the same one earlier rounds saw with the demo mix; it is not new.
- **Keyboard:** Tab and Shift+Tab move through the dialog in the same order as before. The arrow keys skip the disabled video option, and Esc closes the dialog and returns focus to the Export button.
- **Network and console:** no storage or token requests and no `Authorization` headers. The MP3 encoder (from unpkg) loads only after choosing MP3. No hydration warnings or real console errors. The page HTML from the server contains none of the new ids, so they are created only in the browser.
- **Purchase protection holds:** `/studio/middle-east` shows "Sign in required". The anonymous token request returns 401, and the header link opens the demo `/studio-lab`.
- **A's tests:** I re-ran mutations a and f in my own scratch copy and they fail the same tests A reported; the unchanged copy passes 49/49. A's 18 targeted test files (194 tests) all pass.

**Blocked:** the fake-login 403 check returned 500 because the backend isn't available in the cloud. I listed it the same way round 92 did. The full test suite, verify, build and e2e smoke are left to the root gate.

**Ableton:** both behaviours are CZABA's own dialog accessibility and wording, so there is no Ableton comparison to make.

**Notes for B, not bugs:**
- I agree with A's reviewer that the copied test setup (`FakeAudioBuffer` now appears in 61 test files) is worth one small cleanup task.
- In `root-pre-push-review.md`, L6 (the "graph" note being wrong when the loop is on) is covered by the loop texts I tested. M2 (the dialog re-renders on every playback frame) is still open, outside this round.

I deleted the 29 MB exported WAV after reading it; its measurements are saved in `export-1280x720.json`.

Everything is in `tmp/studio-real-loop/`:
- `c-round-93.md`
- `c-round-93.json`
- `c-round-93/` (`out/`, `shots/`, `tools/`, logs)
